mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the next 60 days indicates a shift toward accommodative monetary policy, which lowers discount rates and increases the present value of expected equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day forward returns despite a sustained FEDFUNDS decline, or the 60-day discount rate spread remains positive across all tested regimes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate above 5.5% triggers a risk-off reaction in equity markets, compressing forward discount rates and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day forward returns in a tightening regime despite FEDFUNDS > 5.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over 60 days combined with a rising CPIAUCSL index suggests central banks are easing while inflation remains sticky, which compresses discount rates and increases equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX returns remain negative over 60 days despite FEDFUNDS decline and CPIAUCSL rise, or discount rate spread is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly pay growth acceleration (PAYEMS) above 2% for three consecutive months signals rising labor market confidence, which increases corporate earnings expectations and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX returns remain negative despite PAYEMS > 2% for 3 months, or earnings surprise distribution is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly pay growth deceleration (PAYEMS) below 1% for three consecutive months indicates weakening labor market momentum, which compresses earnings growth expectations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX returns remain negative despite PAYEMS deceleration, or earnings surprise distribution is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly pay growth acceleration (PAYEMS) above 2% combined with a rising UNRATE suggests strong labor market momentum and rising wage inflation, which increases earnings expectations and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX returns remain negative over 60 days despite PAYEMS > 2% and UNRATE rise, or discount rate spread is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production acceleration (INDPRO) above 2% for three consecutive months indicates strengthening supply chain activity, which reduces idiosyncratic uncertainty and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX returns remain negative despite INDPRO acceleration, or idiosyncratic volatility is lower than baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production deceleration (INDPRO) below 0.5% for three consecutive months signals supply-side softness, which increases uncertainty and compresses growth expectations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX returns remain negative despite INDPRO deceleration, or idiosyncratic volatility is higher than baseline.
